body: I faced the issue of missing segments with live content before. The ExoPlayer then performes the configured number of requests for the missing segment, and exits afterwards. It would be great to support skipping segments in that case.

issue.title: loadError

repository.name: ExoPlayer
repository.description: This project is deprecated and stale. The latest ExoPlayer code is available in https://github.com/androidx/media

issue.body:
Hey,

 I have an MPD http://video.vcu.tv/134373_e46fa5a01d4819072a9b53667ff15b2f/134373.mpd, It should be generated with 24 segments but was instead generated with 23.999999998 due to a precision error which happens on some platform if the values get calculated in a certain way.  I have a bug filed with the encoder API to get the precision issue fixed so that 24 are generated as they should.. 

My question here is once the Exo player gets into the load error state, If I hit rewind and seek back to a segment that does exists and was played correctly the player won't play the segment again is this by design or is it something that can be changed ? 

https://gist.github.com/abhiguru/efe59963fc45d1535604

body:
This is confirmed to occur with the [mp4box](https://github.com/gpac/gpac) packager. We have also seen it with various customer content of unknown origin and in our testing with various different products. I do not have a list nor do I remember the specific ones affected, though.

See also discussion here: https://github.com/gpac/gpac/issues/360#issuecomment-170904967

Quick update: there are attempts to raise the topic in MPEG for clarification of what is "the right way" but from what I see right now, CMAF will explicitly state that samples must be provided for the entire timeline, so possibly this issue is becoming less relevant as 404s get even more officially relegated to the "broken content" category.
Thanks for the update. Does this issue still occur with mp4box, or has that been resolved?
The issue still occurs with mp4box.

@erdemguven - It's probably rather easy to handle this in 2.x (`DashChunkSource.onChunkLoadError` could probably handle the error, and then when a subsequent call comes into `DashChunkSource.getNextChunk` requesting the final chunk - we could instead return endOfStream).
Fixed in `dev-v2`, which is the V2 development branch.
